issues.legal_issue: A fresh declaration may be issued after an earlier invalid declaration, and the preliminary acquisition notice remains available when the earlier declaration did not effectively exercise the acquisition power.
material_facts: The first declaration provided that the entire acquisition expense would be borne by a cooperative housing society, although the governing law did not permit acquisition for a public purpose on that basis.
The government cancelled that declaration and later issued a fresh declaration providing for acquisition at public expense for the housing scheme.
The preliminary notice had not fulfilled its purpose because the first declaration was invalid.
issues.conclusion: The earlier declaration was invalid and had no effect; the preliminary notice remained in force, and the government could issue a fresh declaration correcting the funding defect. The successive-declaration rule in State of Madhya Pradesh v. Vishnu Prasad Sharma did not prevent this because the first declaration was invalid.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 4 and 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, read with the proviso to Section 6, compensation for acquisition for a public purpose must be payable wholly or partly from public revenues or a fund controlled or managed by a local authority; the government cannot acquire land for a public purpose where compensation is to be paid entirely by a company. Valjibhai Muljibhai Soneji v. State of Bombay and Girdharilal Amratlal Shodan v. State of Gujarat establish that an invalid declaration may be treated as ineffective and followed by a fresh declaration, and that cancellation recognizing its invalidity does not itself amount to withdrawal from the acquisition. Section 48 does not preclude a fresh declaration in those circumstances. State of Madhya Pradesh v. Vishnu Prasad Sharma, which addresses successive declarations following an effective declaration, does not bar a fresh declaration following an invalid one.

rule.if: land_acquisition_proceeding and first_declaration_invalid_for_private_funding and preliminary_notice_purpose_unfulfilled and fresh_declaration_provides_public_funding

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The matter concerns the acquisition of land by the government.
predicates.first_declaration_invalid_for_private_fu: The government first declared an acquisition for a public purpose with the entire compensation payable by a private body.
predicates.preliminary_notice_purpose_unfulfilled: The preliminary notice had not fulfilled its purpose because the first declaration was invalid.
predicates.fresh_declaration_provides_public_fundin: The government later issued a fresh declaration providing for acquisition at public expense.

issues.definition: When an acquisition proceeding has an invalid first declaration based on entirely private funding, the preliminary notice remains unfulfilled, and a fresh declaration provides for public funding, the fresh declaration is permitted.

issues.legal_issue: Acquisition of land for a cooperative housing scheme can serve a public purpose even when the scheme benefits a limited group of people.
material_facts: The cooperative housing society was formed to enable its members to construct houses.
The government declared that the land was needed for the society's housing scheme.
issues.conclusion: Acquisition of land for the cooperative housing society's housing scheme was for a public purpose; a housing scheme does not cease to be a public purpose merely because it serves a limited number of people.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 4 and 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the government is the best judge of whether the proposed purpose is public, and the needs of a section of the public may constitute a public purpose. Pandit Jhandu Lal v. State of Punjab, Ratilal Shankarbhai v. State of Gujarat, Ram Swarup v. District Land Acquisition Officer, and State of Gujarat v. Musamiyan Imam Haider Bux Razvi support the conclusion that acquisition for a cooperative housing society may be for a public purpose.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The matter concerns the acquisition of land by the government.
predicates.acquisition_for_cooperative_housing: The government sought to acquire land for a cooperative housing scheme.
predicates.scheme_meets_housing_needs_of_a_section_: The scheme was intended to meet housing needs of a section of the public, even if its beneficiaries were limited in number.

issues.definition: When land is acquired for a cooperative housing scheme that meets the housing needs of a section of the public, the acquisition is a public purpose.

issues.legal_issue: Delay in issuing a fresh declaration after cancellation of an invalid declaration does not invalidate the fresh declaration in the circumstances of this case.
material_facts: The landowner challenged the first declaration, which was invalid because the acquisition was to be funded entirely by the cooperative housing society.
The government cancelled the invalid declaration and later issued a fresh declaration providing for acquisition at public expense.
The landowner had not pleaded unreasonable delay in the writ petition, and the interval between cancellation and the fresh declaration was one year and four months.
issues.conclusion: The fresh declaration was not invalid for delay. The landowner had not raised delay as a ground, and the interval between cancellation of the invalid declaration and issuance of the fresh declaration was not unreasonable in the circumstances.
issues.legal_principle: The Land Acquisition Act, 1894 does not preclude a fresh declaration when an earlier declaration is ineffective. Whether delay makes a fresh declaration unreasonable depends on the circumstances, including whether delay was pleaded and whether it was attributable to the challenger. Gujarat State Transport Corporation v. Valji Mulji Soneji was cited in support of the conclusion that a substantial interval may not be unreasonable in the circumstances.

rule.if: land_acquisition_proceeding and earlier_declaration_invalid and government_cancelled_earlier_declaration and fresh_declaration_issued_after_cancellation and delay_not_pleaded

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The matter concerns the acquisition of land by the government.
predicates.earlier_declaration_invalid: The first declaration for the acquisition was legally ineffective.
predicates.government_cancelled_earlier_declaration: The government cancelled the first declaration in recognition of its ineffectiveness.
predicates.fresh_declaration_issued_after_cancellat: The government issued a fresh declaration after cancelling the first declaration.
predicates.delay_not_pleaded: The person challenging the fresh declaration did not plead unreasonable delay as a ground of challenge.

issues.definition: When an acquisition proceeding involves an invalid declaration that the government cancels before issuing a fresh declaration, and the challenger did not plead delay, the fresh declaration is not invalid for delay.
